title: 幾何論約·卷一~卷二 (vol 1)
shelf_note: Du Zhigeng's Jihe lunyue, a Qing abridgement of the Chinese Euclid, here in a Siku Quanshu manuscript copy (block-heart reads 欽定四庫全書). It belongs in a general 'universallibrary' collection; the page is Elements II.5–6.
structure_note: Of 112 records, 107 have OCR. The book field says 107 pages are translated, but the structure count says pages_translated 0, so one of the two counters is wrong (this page is translated). Only 6 pages have a printed number, and on this leaf the block-heart shows only 卷二 with no leaf number visible. The 2 backsteps and 2 repeats are therefore most likely misread or juan-level markers, not a scan splice.

book_verdict: A clean page: the OCR follows the manuscript closely, with only minor slips. The translation renders the end of II.5 and the enunciation of II.6 faithfully, and its letter-mapping note and the gloss of 磬折形 as 'gnomon' are accurate and useful. Nothing an expert would flag on sight, apart from the translated-pages counter mismatch in the metadata.
